title: Create a gross-building area plan with an area and tag from boundary lines
task: Create an area plan bound to the Gross Building area scheme on a level, enclose a region with area boundary lines, place an Area inside it and tag it, then read the computed area. Uses ViewPlan.CreateAreaPlan, AreaScheme.IsGrossBuildingArea, Document.Create.NewAreaBoundaryLine, NewArea and NewAreaTag.

pitfalls.symptom: There is nowhere to place an Area: a view made with ViewPlan.Create (a normal floor plan) will not host areas, and NewArea has no view to accept it.
pitfalls.cause: Areas live only in an area plan, which is bound to an AreaScheme -- not in an ordinary floor plan.
pitfalls.fix: Create the view with ViewPlan.CreateAreaPlan(doc, areaSchemeId, levelId). Find the scheme by iterating OfClass(typeof(AreaScheme)) and testing AreaScheme.IsGrossBuildingArea (fall back to the first scheme for a Rentable-style plan).

pitfalls.symptom: Area.Area comes back 0 and the area has no boundary, though NewArea succeeded.
pitfalls.cause: The area boundary loop is open, or the boundary lines were drawn into the wrong view, so no enclosed region contains the placement point.
pitfalls.fix: Draw a CLOSED loop of NewAreaBoundaryLine(sketchPlane, line, areaView) into the area view av, with a SketchPlane at the level elevation, then doc.Regenerate() before NewArea; pass a UV that lies inside the loop (e.g. its centre).

pitfalls.symptom: Reusing the room-tag pattern -- NewAreaTag(new LinkElementId(area.Id), ...) -- does not compile or picks the wrong overload.
pitfalls.cause: NewAreaTag's signature is (ViewPlan areaView, Area area, UV point): it takes the Area element directly, whereas NewRoomTag takes a LinkElementId because rooms may live in a linked model.
pitfalls.fix: Pass the Area element itself: doc.Create.NewAreaTag(av, area, uv), placing the tag in the same area view.
